label: Telephone poll
quote: The telephone poll finds that 57% of Australian electors think Australia is “heading in the right direction”, while 32% think Australia is “heading in the wrong direction” and 11% can’t say.

label: June 9/10 & 16/17, 2007
quote: Currently, 51.5% of electors think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, 33.5% in the “wrong direction” and 15% are undecided.

label: June 23/24 & June 30/July 1, 2007
quote: Now, 51.5% (unchanged) of electors think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, 31% (down 2.5%) in the “wrong direction” and 17.5% (up 2.5%) are undecided.

label: July 7/8 and 14/15, 2007
quote: Fifty-five per cent – up 4% – of electors think Australia is heading in the right direction, while 30% – down 1% – think Australia is heading in the wrong direction.

label: July 21/22 and 28/29, 2007
quote: Now, 49% (down 6.5%) of electors think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, 33.5% (up 3.5%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” and 17.5% (up 3%) are undecided.

label: August 8/9, 2007
quote: Of all electors surveyed, 51.5% (2.5% higher than the latest face-to-face Morgan Poll conducted July 21/22 & 28/29) think Australia is heading in the right direction, 34.5% think Australia’s heading in the wrong direction, while 14% are undecided.

label: August 4/5 & 11/12, 2007
quote: Now, 49% (unchanged) of electors think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, 34.5% (up 1%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” and 16.5% (down 1%) are undecided.

label: August 18/19 & 25/26, 2007
quote: Now, 48.5% (down 0.5%) of electors think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, 33% (down 1.5%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” and 18.5% (up 2%) are undecided.

label: September 1/2, 2007
quote: Now, 47% (down 1.5%) of electors think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, 34.5% (up 1.5%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” and 18.5% (unchanged) are undecided.

label: September 8/9, 2007
quote: Now, 48% (up 1%) of electors think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, 37% (up 2.5%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” and 15% (down 3.5%) are undecided.

label: September 15/16, 2007
quote: More electors (52.5%, up 4.5%) now think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while fewer (32%, down 5%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 15.5% (up 0.5%) are undecided.

label: September 22/23, 2007
quote: A majority of electors (52%, down 0.5%) think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while 32% (unchanged) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 16% (up 0.5%) are undecided.

label: September 29/30, 2007
quote: Less than half the number of electors (49.5%, down 2.5%) think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while 34.5% (up 2.5%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 16% (unchanged) are undecided.

label: October 6/7, 2007
quote: A majority of electors (53%, up 3.5%) think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while 28.5% (down 6%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 18.5% (up 2.5%) are undecided.

label: October 13/14, 2007
quote: Now, 53% (down 4.5%) think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while 31.5% (up 2.5%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 15.5% (up 2%) are undecided.

label: October 20/21, 2007
quote: Now, 53.5% (down 4%) think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while 30% (up 1%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 16.5% (up 3%) are undecided.

label: October 27/28, 2007
quote: Now, 56% (up 2.5%) think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while 30% (unchanged) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 14% (down 2.5%) are undecided.

label: November 3/4, 2007
quote: Fifty per cent (down 6%) thought Australia was heading in the “right direction”, while 30.5% (up 0.5%) thought Australia was heading in the “wrong direction” — 19.5% (up a significant 5.5%) were undecided.

label: November 7/8, 2007
quote: Now, 55.5% (down 8%) think Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while 31% (up 3%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 13.5% (up 5%) are undecided.

label: November 10/11, 2007
quote: A majority of electors (55.5%, unchanged) think Australia is heading in the “right direction”; while 29% (down 2%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction”, with 15% (up 2%) undecided.

label: November 15-17, 2007
quote: With both major political parties ‘bombarding’ voters with largely negative advertising on industrial relations, union power and interest rates, fewer Australians (48%, down 7.5%) now believe Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while 37% (up 8%) — the highest result since early September — think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 15% (down 0.5%) are undecided.

label: November 23, 2007
quote: A majority of electors (54%, up 2%) now believe Australia is heading in the “right direction”, while 30% (down 4%) think Australia is heading in the “wrong direction” — 16% (up 2%) are undecided.

label: Latest Roy Morgan survey of national sentiment
quote: Back home, the latest Roy Morgan survey of national sentiment recorded a “big” 11% fall in the group who see Australia headed in the “right direction”, down to 51%. 29.5% (up 9.5%) think the country is “seriously heading in the wrong direction” (19% can’t say where it’s headed. We call them the supporters of Malcolm Turnbull.)

label: Latest Morgan poll, taken last weekend
quote: However, 54% of people polled (up 4.5%) thought “Australia is heading in the right direction”, while 27% (down 3%) believe “Australia is heading in the wrong direction”.

label: January 9/10 & 16/17, 2010
quote: The Roy Morgan Government Confidence Rating is now at 136.5 (up 4pts) with 59.5% (up 1%) of Australians confident that Australia is ‘heading in the right direction,’ compared to 23% (down 3%) that say Australia is ‘heading in the wrong direction.’
